scenarios.draft: Test admin ability to list discussion board channels using search and pagination filters. Verify correct results when filtering by code, name, description, position, active status, created_at, and updated_at. Check that pagination works as expected when specifying page size and page number. Confirm that channels with both active=true and active=false can be located. Include edge cases where no channels match the filter, and where results cross page boundaries. Failures include invalid filter values or unauthorized access attempt.

Verify that searching for channels with filters that do not match any records returns an empty list, not an error. For example, filter with a unique, non-existing name or code string. Confirm that the response structure is consistent and paginated, but contains no data rows.

Confirm that a non-admin or unauthenticated user is denied access to the channel listing endpoint. Attempt to call the endpoint without admin role and validate that the proper authorization error is returned.

Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of administrator assignments from the system. Simulate use by an admin managing platform access or conducting an audit. Provide search/filter criteria such as assigned_by_admin_id or a specific time range, and verify that the endpoint correctly returns only those assignments matching the criteria. Also test pagination by requesting multiple pages. Ensure the response contains only records as per the schema, and that irrelevant or out-of-schema fields are ignored. Verify that role-based access controls restrict access to authorized admins only. Edge cases should include empty result sets and invalid filter criteria.

dependencies.purpose: Create member accounts to serve as admins and users for assignment relationships.
Assign admin privileges to members so there are records to search and filter.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a single administrator assignment by a valid id. Simulate an audit or access control workflow where a specific admin assignment needs to be reviewed. Confirm that data matches the assignment that was previously created, and that only fields defined in the schema are returned.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member to be assigned admin privileges.
Grant admin assignment to the created member, capture the assignment id for retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test the behavior when requesting an admin assignment by an ID that does not exist. Provide an obviously invalid UUID or a well-formed but non-existent id, and expect a 404 error or appropriate error response. Confirm that no sensitive data is leaked and that error messaging follows platform conventions.

Test retrieving a paginated, filtered list of notification log records with combination filters and sorting. First, create multiple notifications of various types (e.g., announcement, user_mention), with different delivery statuses and target_id values. Then, search using filters such as target_id, type, delivered=true/false, and created_at range. Confirm only matching records are returned. Validate pagination and edge cases (such as requesting a page with no results), as well as permission enforcement for admin and moderator roles.

dependencies.purpose: Create a variety of notification log records with different types, delivery statuses, and target/member relationships to enable realistic filtering and searching.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving details for a single notification log record by id. First, create a notification using the API to obtain a valid id. Fetch the notification and validate that all schema fields are present and accurate. Then, attempt to fetch a notification by a non-existent or invalid id and verify the system returns a 404 error, confirming robust error handling. Permission enforcement for admin and moderator roles must be validated.

dependencies.purpose: Create a notification log record and retrieve its id for detail-fetching tests.

scenarios.draft: Test creating a notification log entry with valid required data (type, title, delivered, and optionally target_id and body). Validate that the returned record contains all expected schema fields with correct values and generated metadata. Additionally, attempt creation with missing required fields (e.g., omit title or type) or with an invalid type value, and check that the API returns validation errors. Confirm only admin users can successfully create notifications and that attempts by unauthorized users are rejected.

Test repeatedly creating notifications of the same type for the same target_id (if supported by business rules). Ensure the API allows multiple notifications if the schema permits, or returns a uniqueness/conflict error if not. This validates deduplication or idempotency logic.

Test updating a notification log entry by id, altering allowed fields (type, title, body, delivered, delivered_at, and target_id). Ensure the update is applied and returned record reflects changes. Attempt to update immutable fields (id, created_at) and confirm the API returns a validation or error response, as those should not be updated. Also attempt update for a non-existent id and assert that a 404 is returned. Confirm only admins can update, and unauthorized attempts are denied.

dependencies.purpose: Create a notification log to update and verify update behavior with valid/invalid attempts.

scenarios.draft: Test permanent deletion of a notification log entry by id. First, create a notification log and delete it, confirming success by checking the entry is no longer retrievable by id. Attempt to delete a non-existent id to confirm a 404 is correctly returned. Confirm that only admins are permitted to perform deletion actions and that other roles or unauthenticated attempts are rejected.

dependencies.purpose: Establish a notification log entry to target for the deletion test.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a list of comment snapshots with different filtering and pagination parameters. Cover searching by comment id, member id, post id, specific version, and snapshot_created_at range to ensure all supported filters work. Also test pagination edge cases like page size boundaries and requesting a page beyond available data. Verify results only contain schema-defined fields and that invalid or unsupported filters result in appropriate error responses.

dependencies.purpose: Create test comments to ensure there are comments with associated snapshots for filtering.
Create multiple comment snapshot versions tied to different comments and members to test filtering and pagination.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a single comment snapshot record by its id. Confirm that for a valid id, all schema fields are returned and match creation. Attempt retrieval with a non-existent or invalid UUID, and verify a not-found or validation error is returned as appropriate.

dependencies.purpose: Create a base comment for associating snapshots.
Create a comment snapshot and extract its id for successful lookup. Also, ensure there are no records for an invalid id request.

scenarios.draft: Test creating a comment snapshot with all required and optional schema-compliant properties: discussionboard_comment_id, discussionboard_member_id, discussionboard_post_id, body, version, and snapshot_created_at. Verify that creation succeeds and the resulting record matches input. Then, try omitting required fields or providing invalid foreign keys to confirm the system returns validation or constraint errors.

dependencies.purpose: Create a valid comment to obtain a discussionboard_comment_id and post_id for the snapshot.
Create or retrieve a member record for use as the editor (discussionboard_member_id) in the snapshot.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a comment snapshot record by id using a full replacement payload with valid schema fields. Confirm that changes are reflected correctly. Attempt updates using invalid ids, non-existent fields, or data that violates constraints to check error handling. If field updates are not allowed for some schema fields (business constraints), ensure appropriate error is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment to associate with a new comment snapshot.
Create or use a member account for the snapshot update scenario.
Create a comment snapshot to obtain a valid id for update testing.

scenarios.draft: Test permanent deletion of a comment snapshot by its id. After deletion, attempt to retrieve the same snapshot to ensure it is no longer accessible (not found error). Also, try deleting with an invalid id and check that appropriate error or status is returned. Ensure no soft-delete logic is used and the removal is irreversible.

dependencies.purpose: Create a base comment for generating a snapshot to be deleted.
Create and then delete a comment snapshot in the test cycle.

scenarios.draft: Simulate an admin user listing all system configuration records using various search and filter options. Provide request examples that filter by key, value, active status, created_at range, etc., confirming only fields existing in the schema are utilized. Verify pagination works and all listed fields match the expected schema (id, key, value, description, created_at, updated_at).

Test the scenario where an admin requests a list of configuration rows with filters that do not match any records (e.g., a nonexistent key or value), ensuring an empty result set is returned, with appropriate pagination metadata.
Check that an admin can retrieve the second page of configuration list results when a page limit is set, and confirm both total record count and pagination fields are present and correct.
Test retrieving a configuration row by valid id as an admin. First, create a configuration record and then retrieve it by its id. Verify all schema-defined fields are returned in detail.

dependencies.purpose: Create a configuration to obtain a valid id for lookup.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a configuration row with an id that does not exist. Ensure the API returns an appropriate not found error (404), and no extra/non-schema fields are returned in the response.

Test successful creation of a system configuration record by an admin, ensuring all required fields (key, value) are set and key uniqueness is enforced. Provide valid payload, check the response for all expected fields, and validate their values.

Test creation failure when attempting to create a configuration with a key that already exists in the system. First, create a configuration record, then attempt to create another with the same key; verify a duplicate key error is returned and no new record is added.

dependencies.purpose: Create initial configuration with a specific key to trigger duplicate scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test validation failure when required fields (e.g., key or value) are omitted from the configuration create request. Confirm the API returns a validation error and no record is created.

Test updating a system configuration's value and optional description by id as an admin. First, create a configuration, then update its value and/or description. Verify that key and id fields remain unchanged and response contains the updated values only for allowed modifiable fields.

dependencies.purpose: Create configuration for update testing.

scenarios.draft: Validate that updating an existing configuration while attempting to change the key field results in a validation error, as the key is immutable. Confirm the API prohibits the change and the original value remains intact.

dependencies.purpose: Create configuration to obtain id for this failed update scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a configuration with a non-existent id value. Ensure that the system returns an appropriate not found error and no changes are made.
Verify that an admin can permanently delete a configuration record by id. First, create a configuration, then delete it, and confirm it cannot be found afterwards using the GET endpoint.

dependencies.purpose: Create configuration record to then delete.

scenarios.draft: Ensure attempting to delete a configuration record with a non-existent id returns a not found error and does not affect existing configurations.

Test listing of audit logs with multiple types of filters and pagination: by actor_id (admin), by action type (e.g., 'delete', 'edit'), by date range, and using pagination parameters. Verify that only logs matching the filters are returned in the paginated format, and confirm correct handling of no results. Also test edge case: invalid filter values should return validation errors rather than logs.

Test retrieving a single audit log record by valid id and confirm all expected schema fields are present. Next, try with a non-existent or malformed id and verify a 404 or validation error is returned. This covers the common admin or moderator review workflow and correct error signaling when the log is not found.

dependencies.purpose: Create a test member, who can then be the actor in an audit log.
Generate an actual audit log record associated with a valid actor_id for fetch testing.

scenarios.draft: Test the creation of an audit log record with valid payload: valid actor_id (existing member/admin), action type, optional target_id and payload, and confirm that the new log record is returned. Then, attempt creation with missing required fields (e.g., actor_id or action missing) and with invalid actor_id (non-existent) to ensure validation errors are triggered. Verify all required audit fields are persisted and that database constraints (e.g., valid UUIDs) are enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Create a valid member or admin to use as the actor_id for the audit log creation.

scenarios.draft: Test updating the payload field of an existing audit log (simulating adding more context or correction) as an admin. Ensure changes are persisted and the updated record is returned. Attempt update of non-permitted fields such as action or actor_id, which should be rejected with a validation error. Also attempt to update a non-existent audit log id to confirm a 404 or error is produced. Confirm only payload or permitted fields are affected and audit compliance is preserved.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin who will have the appropriate permissions.
Create an audit log record to be updated.

scenarios.draft: Test hard deleting an audit log record as an admin by id; verify that the record is permanently removed and no longer retrievable. Additionally, attempt to delete a non-existent audit log id and confirm that the system returns a suitable error message (e.g., 404 not found). Ensure that only authorized users (admins) can perform this operation and unauthorized/delegated users are denied access if attempted (if role simulation is supported in the test suite).

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin member to perform the delete operation.
Create an audit log record for deletion, ensuring there is a known valid id.

scenarios.draft: Test listing comments with various filters, including by post association, author, parent comment, nesting, and date/time windows. Explore edge cases such as requesting comments for a post with no comments, searching by deleted (soft-deleted) comments, and ensuring paginated results are correctly limited and ordered. Also verify that all returned fields match the schema and soft-deleted comments correctly expose the deleted_at value. Required setup includes creating posts and comments, some marked as deleted, to satisfy filter scenarios.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post entity to serve as parent for the test comments.
Create multiple comments with various parent/child and soft-delete states for search coverage.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a specific comment by its unique id. Include cases for a valid existing comment, as well as a comment that has been soft-deleted (deleted_at set). Ensure all schema fields are returned and deleted_at accurately reflects deletion status. Attempt to get a comment with a non-existent id to verify not found error handling. Valid setup requires at least one normal comment and one soft-deleted comment.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post for associating comments.
Create comments, at least one of which is later soft deleted for test coverage.
Soft delete a comment to enable retrieval testing of deleted record.

scenarios.draft: Test the creation of a new comment both as a root-level comment (with no parent_id) and as a reply to an existing comment (using parent_id). Validate required fields such as discussionboard_post_id and discussionboard_member_id. Test error cases such as invalid or missing references (nonexistent post/member/parent), and try to create a comment referencing a non-existent parent_id to trigger foreign key validation error. All created comment entities should match the schema. Setup steps include creating the post and member, and creating an initial comment to allow reply testing.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post to be associated with the comment.
Create a member who will serve as the comment author.

scenarios.draft: Test updating an existing comment's body and, if applicable, its parent_id. Try changing the body to a new value as well as re-parenting the comment (changing parent_id). Validate that forbidden operations, like referencing a non-existent parent comment, are properly rejected. Perform update for a non-existent comment id to verify error handling. Success responses should return fully updated comment objects per schema. Setup requires pre-creation of initial comment tree and parent options.

dependencies.purpose: Create the parent post for comment association.
Create a member as comment author.
Create multiple comments to establish initial structure for parent_id change testing.

scenarios.draft: Test soft-deleting an existing comment by setting its deleted_at to the current server time. Verify success case and confirm the deleted_at field is set. Attempt to delete the same comment again to confirm idempotent behavior (deleted_at should be updated again or left as is). Also, test deleting a non-existent comment (id not found). Ensure that no data is hard deleted. Setup requires a valid comment available for deletion.

dependencies.purpose: Create post for comment association.
Create member for comment author.
Create a comment for soft-delete testing.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an admin or moderator can retrieve a paginated and filtered list of discussionboard_moderation_actions. This includes searching by action type, acting_moderator_id, or report_id, and paginating results to inspect UI/dashboard usage. Ensure valid filters return correct moderation actions, pagination metadata is present, and invalid filter values are handled gracefully (e.g., nonexistent moderator ID, incorrect action type). Edge cases like empty results, first/last page navigation, and invalid pagination values (negative or zero page/limit) must also be tested.

Test retrieval of a specific moderation action by its unique id. First, create a moderation action (using POST /discussionboard/moderationActions) and capture its id. Fetch it using the GET endpoint and verify that all fields match the created record. This scenario ensures accurate, end-to-end retrieval.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderation action and obtain its id for retrieval testing.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to retrieve a moderation action using an id that does not exist in the database. Confirm that the system responds with a not found error, and no entity details are leaked. This tests proper error handling and information security for missing ids.

Test the successful creation of a moderation action. Prepare valid data including a real acting_moderator_id, a report_id (if applicable), target_object_type and id, action_type, rationale, and actioned_at. Ensure all referenced foreign keys exist (e.g., moderator, report, target object) by creating them if needed. Upon POST, verify the returned entity matches input and all required fields are present. This validates end-to-end workflow for creating a moderation action.

Attempt to create a moderation action with one or more required fields missing (e.g., omit action_type or acting_moderator_id). Confirm that the API responds with a validation error, preventing incomplete moderation actions from being created. Validate that no partial record is saved, and error details are informative.

Try creating a moderation action with invalid foreign key references such as a non-existent acting_moderator_id or report_id. Confirm that the API rejects the request and returns an appropriate foreign key constraint error, ensuring referential integrity. No moderation action should be created in this case.

Test the ability to update details of a moderation action by id. Initially create a test action (POST), then use PUT with new values for action_type, rationale, or target_object_type. After updating, retrieve the action and verify all updates were correctly applied. Ensure that only allowed fields are modifiable and immutable fields remain unchanged.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderation action to be updated later.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to update a moderation action using a non-existent id. Verify that the API returns a not found error, with no changes to the database. This ensures that updates only affect valid, existing actions.

Try updating a moderation action using an invalid field value (e.g., prohibited action_type, malformed rationale, or missing required property). Confirm that the server responds with validation errors and no update is applied if the data does not meet schema requirements.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderation action so invalid update scenarios can be applied to a real record.

scenarios.draft: Test deleting a moderation action by its id. First, create a moderation action (POST), then delete it using the DELETE endpoint. Afterwards, attempt to retrieve the deleted action and make sure it cannot be found (ensuring true hard delete). This scenario verifies deletion and non-recoverability.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderation action to be deleted.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to delete a moderation action using a non-existent id. The server should return a not found error and not affect any existing records. This ensures deletion logic is safe against invalid or malicious requests.

Test that an admin or moderator can retrieve a paginated, filtered list of ban records. Provide various filter combinations, such as filtering by acting_moderator_id, banned_member_id, report_id, ban_type, reason, banned_at, and expires_at. Confirm the correct bans are returned according to filter criteria. Vary pagination parameters to validate correct page and limit processing. Also test that filtering by a nonexistent member or ban_type returns no records. Check behavior when no filter is provided (all bans returned, paginated).

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple ban records with differing properties—acting_moderator_id, banned_member_id, types, date ranges, and reasons—to be used in filter and pagination tests.
Create one or more member records to use as acting moderator and banned member for bans.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving full details of a ban record by providing a valid ban id. The response should contain exactly the schema-defined fields (id, banned_member_id, acting_moderator_id, report_id, reason, ban_type, banned_at, expires_at).

dependencies.purpose: Create a ban record and obtain its id for use in the detail query.

scenarios.draft: Test that requesting a ban record by a non-existent id results in a 404 or similar not-found error.

Test creation of a new ban record with all required fields and optionally with report_id and expires_at fields set to verify extended use cases and schema compliance. Confirm that the returned ban has all properties stored and that the side effects (e.g., user restrictions) are handled by application logic, not the API. Validate that required fields cause validation failure if omitted.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to be banned (banned_member_id).
Create an admin or moderator account for acting_moderator_id.

scenarios.draft: Test that attempts to create a ban with a nonexistent banned_member_id, acting_moderator_id, or report_id result in a foreign key constraint validation error. Test that creating a duplicate ban with same member within an overlapping ban period is rejected according to business rules, if applicable.

dependencies.purpose: Create members to use as reference for negative test cases.

scenarios.draft: Test updating an existing ban with changes to reason, ban_type, expires_at, or report_id. Validate that the updated values are reflected in the returned entity. Also attempt to update a non-existent ban id and expect a not-found error. Validate that setting invalid banned_member_id or acting_moderator_id in update results in an error due to failing foreign key constraints.

dependencies.purpose: Create an initial ban record to update in success scenarios.
Create additional member(s) in order to test reference updates or errors.

scenarios.draft: Test deleting an existing ban by id: after deletion, the record should not be retrievable and is permanently removed. Also attempt to delete a non-existent ban id and expect a not-found error. Check that deletion does not impact the member's other roles or related entities—only this ban entry is removed.

dependencies.purpose: Create a ban record to subsequently delete in the test.

scenarios.draft: Admin requests a paginated list of report types to populate the moderation dashboard's report reason select box. The request seeks only active report types and sorts by created_at descending order. Confirm that the response contains only schema-validated fields and correctly paginates the result set. Also test with a filter for inactive report types (active=false) and confirm that only those types are returned. Edge case: filter by a display_name containing a rare string; verify empty result is handled gracefully.
Test searching report types with an unsupported filter property (not in schema) to verify the API rejects such requests with an appropriate validation error.

Fetch a report type by its id. First, create a report type so a valid id is guaranteed. Then, retrieve details using this id and confirm all schema fields are returned, including code, display_name, description, active, and created_at.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new report type to guarantee a valid id exists for retrieval testing.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to fetch a report type using a non-existent or random UUID. Confirm the API returns a 404 error, indicating no such report type is present.

Create a new report type (e.g., 'abuse') with code, display_name, description, active flag, and created_at. Ensure the request uses only schema-fields and that creation is successful with all values correctly persisted and returned in the response.

Attempt to create a report type with a code that already exists in the system. First, create a report type with a unique code. Then, try to create another report type using that same code. Expect a validation error indicating that the code must be unique.

dependencies.purpose: Create the initial report type with a unique code to trigger a duplicate on the second creation.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to create a report type missing one or more required fields (e.g., no code or display_name). Confirm that the API returns a validation error specifying which required fields are absent.

Update the display_name and active flag of an existing report type. Create a report type first, then update its display_name and active status. Confirm the response correctly reflects the updated values without altering unmodified fields like code or created_at.

dependencies.purpose: Create a report type to be updated during the test.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to update an existing report type's code to the code value of another report type (while code should be updatable if schema allows). Set up by creating two report types with different codes, then update the second one to try and match the first's code. Expect a uniqueness violation error or schema-driven rejection if code editing is forbidden by schema/business logic.

dependencies.purpose: Create the first report type with an initial code.
Create the second report type whose code will be updated to duplicate the first.

scenarios.draft: Try updating a report type with a request that includes fields not present in the schema. API should reject such properties and return a validation error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a report type to update in the test.

scenarios.draft: Delete a report type by id. First, create a report type, then delete it. Confirm the API responds with success confirmation and subsequent fetches by the same id return 404 or not found.

dependencies.purpose: Create a report type to delete by id in this test.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to delete a report type by a non-existent id. Confirm the API bounces the request with an error, such as 404 not found, as the report type does not exist.

Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of thread tag assignments by calling the list endpoint with different filter, sort, and pagination parameters. Verify that results include the correct tag assignments based on thread_id, assigned_at range, and removed_at (for both active and historical tags). Validate correct pagination (page/size), sorting, and schema compliance. Edge cases: empty result when filters don't match, maximum page size, invalid sort value. Ensure results only expose schema fields.

dependencies.purpose: Create a thread to assign tags to and act as a target for filter testing.
Assign multiple tags to the thread so there is data to search/filter/paginate in the tag assignment list.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a specific thread tag assignment by its id. First, create a thread and assign a tag to it, then fetch that tag assignment by its returned id to verify all fields are present and correct. Edge cases: attempt to fetch a thread tag assignment with an invalid or non-existent id and confirm that a not found error is returned.

Create (assign) a thread tag to the thread, so that the tag assignment id can be queried.

Verify the creation is successful and the returned entity contains correct schema fields. dependencies.purpose: Create a thread to assign a tag for the positive test cases.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a thread tag assignment by its id. Scenario 2: Attempt to update other permitted fields, such as assigned_at, for audit correction, and validate changes are applied. dependencies.purpose: Create a thread and assign a tag to generate a valid tag assignment id for update.
Assign a tag to the thread so that the created tag assignment can be updated.

scenarios.draft: Test hard deleting a thread tag assignment by id. Scenario 1: Delete an existing assignment after creation and verify the record is permanently removed (subsequent GET returns not found). Scenario 2: Attempt to delete a thread tag assignment that does not exist and verify the system returns the correct error message. Confirm that deleting the assignment does not affect the associated thread record or other tags.

dependencies.purpose: Create a thread and assign a tag for deletion testing.
Create a thread tag assignment to be deleted.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieval of a paginated and filtered list of moderation reports by supplying various filter parameters such as report type, reporting member, moderation target, status, and different date ranges. This scenario ensures reports can be searched and paged as intended for moderation workflows. Validate proper inclusion of relevant reports based on supplied filters, and verify that invalid or unsupported filter fields are rejected with appropriate errors.

dependencies.purpose: Create several moderation reports with known types, members, and targets to serve as test data for list and search operations.

scenarios.draft: Test listing moderation reports using search filters that should produce zero results (e.g., future date range or a non-existent reporter ID). Ensure the API returns an empty list and does not fail or throw errors for valid but unmatched queries.

dependencies.purpose: Create at least one moderation report, ensuring there are baseline records for negative filtering.

scenarios.draft: Test the moderation report listing endpoint with a filter field not present in the schema. Confirm the API responds with a validation error describing the unsupported field, ensuring strict schema adherence.

Test retrieval of a specific moderation report by its ID. The test should ensure that all expected fields are accurately returned for a valid report, and the data matches what was created. This supports use cases such as moderation review and workflow escalation.

dependencies.purpose: Create a sample moderation report and extract its ID for targeted retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test the API's error handling when attempting to fetch a moderation report with a non-existent or deleted ID. The endpoint should return a 404 not found error or equivalent, confirming proper error semantics for missing records.

Test successful creation of a new moderation report by providing all required fields (report type, reporting member, target object ID/type, description, and reported_at). Validate that the API returns the complete new report record and matches input data, and that the report becomes retrievable via the GET endpoint.

Attempt to create a moderation report omitting one of the required schema fields (such as target_object_type or report_type). Validate that the API rejects the request with a validation error specifying the missing field, and no record is created.

Test a full update of an existing moderation report record, modifying updatable fields such as report type, description, or target object references. Confirm the new values are reflected accurately in the response and persisted for future retrieval. This scenario ensures that update operations replace only schema-defined content and return the updated record as per contract.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderation report to serve as the update target.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to update a moderation report providing an ID for a non-existent report. Validate that the API returns a not found error, and no unintended record is created or modified.

Attempt to update a moderation report by including fields that are not defined in the schema (e.g., unauthorized or additional payload). Confirm the API rejects the update with an appropriate validation error referencing the bad field(s).

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderation report so an existing ID is available for the invalid update test.

scenarios.draft: Test deletion (hard delete) of a moderation report using a valid ID. Confirm that the record is permanently removed by attempting to retrieve it afterward, and that downstream listing does not include the deleted report. Validate correct deletion workflow for administrative cleanup scenarios.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderation report to use as the delete target.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to delete a moderation report with a non-existent or already deleted ID. Verify that the API returns a suitable not found error, and no error or side effect occurs for unrelated records.

Verify the response includes only schema-defined fields (id, version, effective_date, title, content, created_at, updated_at), contains accurate pagination metadata, and matches the query filters. Confirm that no deleted or archived records are returned, as soft delete is unsupported. Test edge cases: empty results (where filter finds none), default pagination, and invalid filter values (should return error or empty list).

Test retrieving the details of a specific privacy policy by a valid id. First, create a new privacy policy, then fetch it by its id. Confirm that the response contains all schema fields and matches the originally created policy's data.

dependencies.purpose: Create a privacy policy to obtain a known valid id for retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test the scenario where a privacy policy is requested by an id that does not exist. Use a random or deleted UUID to ensure the system returns a 404 or appropriate error, and does not expose any sensitive or irrelevant data. This verifies proper error handling for resource absence.

Test successful creation of a new privacy policy record using all required fields (version, effective_date, title, content).
