Verify that updates are reflected in the persisted record and returned values match the request. Confirm that attempts to update immutable or nonexistent fields are rejected. Also, ensure that only authorized roles (admin, moderator) can perform updates.

dependencies.purpose: Create member and moderator accounts for use in warning and update operations.
Create a warning record to be updated.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a warning by providing an invalid or non-existent id, and confirm that the service returns an appropriate not found error. Also, try updates with invalid or missing required fields and verify that validation errors occur with no changes saved.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure there is a warning record to verify not found cases by using an id that is altered or removed.

scenarios.draft: Test deleting a warning record by its id as an authorized user (admin or moderator). First, create a warning, delete it by id, and then confirm the record is no longer retrievable. Ensure that deletion is permanent (hard delete) and no fields are recoverable by GET request afterward. Also verify that the delete operation does not affect unrelated warnings or members.

dependencies.purpose: Issue a warning to be deleted in the test.

scenarios.draft: Test that deletion cannot be performed by unauthorized users (ordinary member or unauthenticated caller) and the system blocks the operation with an appropriate error. Also, attempt to delete a warning by providing a non-existent or malformed id, and check that the service returns a not found or validation error, confirming robust error handling.

dependencies.purpose: Issue a warning to test access control and deletion with a valid existing id.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a list of discussion board settings using complex pagination and filtering options (such as filtering by scope_type, key, and active status). Ensure the result is paginated correctly, only includes records that match filters, and includes all appropriate schema fields. Scenario covers admin using management UI to search for all settings with specific feature flag keys or scope types for configuration auditing.

dependencies.purpose: At least one settings record must be created to ensure there is data to query. Preferably, create several with varied scope_type, key, and active flags for full test coverage.

scenarios.draft: Test successfully retrieving the details of a specific settings record by its id. Confirm that all schema fields are present in the response. Business case: Admin needs to review or update a precise feature toggle or per-area configuration.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new settings record first to get a valid id for detail retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test requesting a detailed settings record using a nonexistent or deleted id. Verify that the response yields the correct not found error, as per schema/business rules, and no sensitive data is leaked.

Test creating a new settings record with all valid business fields (scope_type, key, value, description, position, active, etc). Confirm the response returns all expected schema fields and values match the input. Use case: Admin bootstraps a new feature toggle or per-board rule.

Test attempting to create a settings record with a key and scope_type combination that already exists in the database. Confirm that the unique constraint is enforced and the API returns an appropriate error message describing the conflict.

dependencies.purpose: Create the initial setting with the key and scope_type to establish uniqueness. Then, attempt to create a duplicate to verify error scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test the failure scenario where one or more required fields (like key or scope_type) are omitted from the request. Confirm the API responds with validation errors, listing the missing fields as per schema restrictions.

Test updating an existing settings record with valid fields (such as changing value or description). Confirm the response correctly reflects all updated values, and all constraints are enforced (e.g., key and scope_type remain unique).

dependencies.purpose: Create a new settings record to update, so a valid id and initial data are guaranteed.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a nonexistent settings record by id. Confirm the system responds with the appropriate not found error and does not alter any other records.

Test attempting to update a setting's key/scope_type to a value that collides with another existing setting in the same scope. Ensure the uniqueness constraint triggers the correct error and prevents the update.

dependencies.purpose: Create two settings with different keys and scope_types, so one can be set up for a duplicate collision during update.

scenarios.draft: Test permanently deleting a settings record given a valid id. Confirm the record is no longer retrievable afterward, and deletion confirmation is returned as expected. Scenario simulates admin cleaning up obsolete or test data for compliance.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new settings record so there is a known valid id to delete.

scenarios.draft: Test attempting to delete a settings record using a nonexistent or already deleted id. Confirm the API responds gracefully with a not found or equivalent error, and no unintended data changes occur.

Verify that the API returns a paginated, filterable list of comment votes, filtered by specific comment ID and/or member ID. Scenario: First, create one or more comments and members with upvotes/downvotes. Then, retrieve comment votes using filter parameters (such as a specific comment ID or member ID) and check that only the matching votes are returned. Also test pagination parameters (such as page size, offset) to validate correct paging and total count information. Edge case: Request a filter for a non-existent comment ID—ensure the result is an empty set with no error.

dependencies.purpose: Create one or more comments to allow voting actions to be tested and votes to be filtered by these comment IDs.
Create members who will be used to cast comment votes.
Create upvote and downvote records to ensure vote filtering produces expected results.

scenarios.draft: Test that fetching a comment vote by its valid ID returns the correct vote record. Setup: Create a comment and a member, register a new vote, then attempt to fetch that vote by its ID. Validate that all fields are correct, including vote type and associations. Also, test fetching by a non-existent vote ID should return a 404 or appropriate error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment to be voted on.
Create a member to perform the voting.
Register a new vote so it can be retrieved by ID.

scenarios.draft: Test successful creation of a comment vote given valid data: an existing comment and member, with a valid vote_type value. Then, attempt to create a second vote for the same (comment, member) pair, expecting a unique constraint violation error. Edge cases: Try an invalid vote_type or a vote referencing a non-existent comment/member. Verify that validation errors are reported appropriately. Also, verify that after deleting a previous vote for the same pair, a new vote can be registered.

dependencies.purpose: Create one or more comments that will be voted upon.
Create members who will cast votes.

scenarios.draft: Test updating an existing comment vote's vote_type (e.g., changing upvote to downvote or withdrawing a vote). Scenario: Create a comment, a member, and a vote. Update the vote's type and verify the vote reflects the new value. Attempt to update the vote to reference a different comment or member, violating the uniqueness constraint, and validate that this is rejected. Try updating a non-existent comment vote by ID and check that an appropriate error is returned. Edge case: Provide an invalid vote_type value and expect a validation error.

dependencies.purpose: Create the comment to be voted on.
Create member to cast the vote.
Create an initial vote record to be updated.

scenarios.draft: Test permanently deleting a comment vote by its ID. Scenario: Create a comment, member, and a vote; then perform the delete operation. Confirm that the vote record is no longer retrievable. Additionally, attempt to delete a non-existent vote ID and ensure an appropriate error or status is returned. Business edge-case: Try deleting a vote and then immediately recreating a vote for the same (comment, member, vote_type) tuple to verify that deletion frees the unique constraint for creating a future vote.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment for voting and logical deletion.
Create member to use for the vote.
Create the vote to be deleted and then validated as deleted.

scenarios.draft: Test listing moderator assignments using different filter and pagination parameters. Scenario includes retrieving all moderator assignments, filtering by member_id, by assigned_by_admin_id, and by assignments that are currently active (revoked_at is null or in the future). The system should return paginated lists matching the search criteria and only include records strictly adhering to the schema. Failure case: using an invalid filter field should result in a validation error. Success cases validate correct results for legitimate filter combinations.

dependencies.purpose: Create member records to be eligible as moderator and admin for assignment search filter.
Assign a moderator role to the member so the assignment can be listed in response.

scenarios.draft: Test fetching moderator assignment detail by id. Success: create a moderator assignment, then retrieve it by id and verify all fields (including member_id, assigned_by_admin_id, timestamps, etc.) are present and correct. Failure: attempt to fetch using a non-existent id, expect a 404 not-found error response.

dependencies.purpose: Set up member and admin accounts for assignment relationships.
Assign a moderator role to a created member to produce a valid id for detail retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test assigning moderator privileges to a member. Success: assign a moderator to a member (provide member_id, assigned_by_admin_id, assigned_at, possible expires_at). Validate that assignment is created with correct data. Error: attempt to assign moderator status to the same member twice, confirm unique constraint violation and expected error response. Error: attempt to assign with invalid admin reference (assigned_by_admin_id not an existing admin), expect failure.

dependencies.purpose: Create member records for both moderator assignee and admin assigner. Both references must exist and admin must have appropriate role prior to assignment.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a moderator assignment by id. Success: update assignment's assigned_by_admin_id (to simulate reassignment), change expires_at to extend/shorten assignment, and set revoked_at to immediately revoke privileges. Confirm changes are reflected. Error: attempt to update a non-existent assignment id returns 404. Error: provide invalid field types or values for timestamps, expect validation error.

dependencies.purpose: Establish member and admin for assignment relationships.
Create the moderator assignment to update in test.

scenarios.draft: Test deleting a moderator assignment by id. Success: create and assign moderator, then delete assignment and verify it is no longer retrievable. Error: attempt to delete an assignment that does not exist, expect a 404 or appropriate error message. Ensure deletion does not affect member status, only the assignment link.

dependencies.purpose: Set up member and admin for assignment creation.
Create a moderator assignment record to be deleted in the test.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a paginated, filtered list of thread snapshots for moderation, audit, or version history display. Create a thread, make several edits (each edit generating a snapshot), and then request thread snapshots filtered by thread_id and paginated with a defined page size. Validate that snapshots match expected edits with correct sequence, actors, and content. Confirm that filtering by actor_id, creation time, or title substring returns correct results. Edge case: request a filter or page that yields no results and verify response is empty as expected.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new thread to allow subsequent snapshot creation and search by thread_id.
Generate several thread snapshots for the created thread, with distinct titles or content to support filtering and pagination scenarios.

scenarios.draft: Test both successful and failure scenarios of fetching a single thread snapshot by its id. First, create a new thread and add a thread snapshot with distinctive content or metadata (e.g., specific title or actor_id). Fetch the snapshot using its id and verify data correctness and completeness. Then attempt to retrieve a snapshot using an invalid or non-existent id and verify that a not found (404) error is returned or that the API handles the missing resource per the business contract.

dependencies.purpose: Create the thread entity for associating the test snapshot.
Create a thread snapshot, so the real id is available for a valid fetch test.

scenarios.draft: Test the creation of a thread snapshot with both valid and invalid data. First, create a thread and a member who acts as the snapshot actor. Attempt to create a snapshot using valid thread_id, actor_id (nullable or not), required title, optional body, and optional reason. Confirm snapshot is persisted and returned fields match expectations. Then, attempt to create a snapshot with missing required fields (like thread_id or title) or using ids that do not exist for related entities, and confirm the appropriate validation or constraint error is returned as per schema rules.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure a valid thread exists for associating the snapshot.
Create a member that can serve as actor_id for the snapshot creation test.

scenarios.draft: Test replacing/updating a thread snapshot's title, body, or reason fields by id. First, create a thread, an actor, and an initial snapshot. Then update the snapshot's title, body, or reason via PUT and confirm updates are reflected (where policy allows). Try modifying actor_id if allowed by schema. Follow with an attempt to update a non-existent snapshot id, confirming appropriate 404 or error response. Edge: try updating required fields with null or invalid values and verify that validation errors are produced as per schema.

dependencies.purpose: Create thread to attach snapshot to.
Create a member as the actor for the snapshot.
Create a snapshot with known, updatable values for the update scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test the permanent deletion of a thread snapshot by its id and verify that the snapshot can no longer be retrieved post-deletion. First, create a thread and a snapshot. Issue a DELETE for the snapshot id. After deletion, attempt to fetch the same snapshot and confirm a not found (404) or equivalent error is returned. Also, attempt to delete a non-existent or already-deleted id to verify proper error handling without side effects. Confirm that deletion is irreversible as there is no soft-delete/recovery supported.

dependencies.purpose: Create a thread for use in snapshot creation.
Create the snapshot to enable deletion and subsequent retrieval tests.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of discussion board members. Provide various combinations of pagination, role, activity status, and creation date filters in the request body. Validate that only allowed, non-sensitive fields (excluding hashed_password) are included in the results. Ensure that filtering and pagination respond appropriately to search conditions (e.g., by role or by activity status) and that excluded sensitive fields are not exposed. Verify edge cases such as an empty result set or invalid filter parameters (e.g., non-existent role) return expected errors or empty lists.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple member accounts with varying roles and is_active status to provide a dataset for search and pagination testing.

scenarios.draft: Test the system's response when passing invalid filter parameters (such as unsupported field names or values) while listing members. The API should return a validation error and not break system logic. This scenario ensures robust parameter validation and prevents unauthorized data access via malformed queries.

Test retrieving detailed information of a discussion board member by their unique id when the member exists. The response should include all profile fields (excluding sensitive credentials like hashed_password) and properly reflect is_active and deleted_at state. Verifies correct business logic for displaying admin/moderator/adminself profile access.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account in order to obtain a valid id for detailed lookup.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving member detail using a non-existent or invalid id. The API should return a 404 or equivalent error. This scenario checks that the system does not leak information about deleted or never-existing users and provides a proper, secure error response.

Test the process of creating a new discussion board member by providing valid, unique username, email, hashed_password, role, and is_active status in the request. The endpoint should return the non-sensitive fields of the new member (excluding hashed_password), and the member should be retrievable via list/search and detail endpoints.

Test attempting to create a new member using a username or email that already exists. The endpoint should fail with a constraint violation. Steps: 1) Create a member with a specific username/email, 2) Attempt to create another with the same username/email, and verify that the system enforces uniqueness and returns a clear error.

dependencies.purpose: Create the initial member account to occupy the username and email for the duplicate test.

scenarios.draft: Test creating a member with missing required fields (e.g., missing username, email, role, or hashed_password). The API should fail with a validation error and not create a new record. This scenario checks that required fields are strictly enforced during account creation and that incomplete requests return clear, actionable errors.

Test successful update of member record fields (such as username, email, role, is_active) by id. The response should return the updated record and reflect the changes. Audit/logging is downstream and not directly validated here, but role/permission effects (if system-enforced) should be respected.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account to obtain a valid id for profile update testing.

scenarios.draft: Test updating an existing member's username or email to a value already used by another user. The system should return a constraint violation and not perform the update. Ensures unique constraints on these fields are enforced both on creation and update.

dependencies.purpose: Create at least two member accounts so that one can be updated to attempt a duplicate username/email.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to update a member using a non-existent id. The API should respond with a not found error and perform no update, ensuring secure handling of invalid identifiers.

Test soft-deleting (setting deleted_at) a member account by id. After this operation, the member should be inaccessible for new logins and excluded from active-user search lists, but remain retrievable by id for audit/compliance. The deletion should not physically remove data. This test includes verifying downstream effects, such as access suspension.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account to obtain a valid id for soft-delete (compliance account removal) testing.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to soft-delete a non-existent or already soft-deleted member account. The system should return an appropriate error message and not alter the database or leak information.

Test successfully listing threads with pagination and filtering. First, a board and a member are created, and several threads are created under that board by that member. The list API is called with board_id and author_member_id filters, and pagination (e.g., page size, offset). The test verifies that only threads meeting the criteria are returned and correct pagination metadata is present.

dependencies.purpose: Create a board to associate threads with.
Create a member who will be the thread author.
Create several threads by the member within the board.

scenarios.draft: Test that the listing API includes soft-deleted threads (where deleted_at is not null) when requested. Create a thread, then soft-delete it through the DELETE endpoint, and call the list API with filters that request soft-deleted threads. Verify the soft-deleted thread appears in results with deleted_at set.

dependencies.purpose: Board where thread is created.
Thread author.
Thread to be soft-deleted.
Perform soft-delete on the thread before listing.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a thread successfully by id. Create a new thread and then fetch it by its id. Confirm all fields (id, board_id, author_member_id, title, body, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) are returned, and the data matches what was created.

dependencies.purpose: Board to associate the thread with.
Author of the thread.
Create the thread to later fetch.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a thread by a non-existent id. Call the endpoint with a random UUID that does not correspond to any thread and expect a 404 error or not found response.
Test retrieving a soft-deleted thread by id. Create and soft-delete a thread, then fetch it using its id. The returned thread should have deleted_at set and the core content fields intact.

dependencies.purpose: Create board for the thread.
Author of the thread.
Create a thread to be soft-deleted.
Soft-delete the thread before retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test creating a new thread with valid board_id, author_member_id, title, and optional body. First, create a board and a member, then make a POST request with all required fields. Verify that the new thread is returned with all correct values and timestamps set.

dependencies.purpose: Create a board for the thread.
Create a member as author.

scenarios.draft: Test error when trying to create a thread using a board_id or author_member_id that does not exist. Attempt to POST with invalid references and verify the system returns a foreign key constraint or not found error.
Test that creating a thread fails when required fields (such as board_id, author_member_id, title) are missing. Omit each in turn and verify validation errors are returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create board for thread as a control case.
Create author for the thread as a control case.

scenarios.draft: Test updating the title and body of a thread. First, create a thread, then update it using PUT and verify changes are reflected and updated_at changes accordingly.

dependencies.purpose: Board for thread.
Thread author.
Create a thread to update.

scenarios.draft: Test soft-deleting and restoring a thread using PUT. Create a thread, update the thread to set deleted_at (simulate soft delete), then update again with deleted_at set to null (restore). Confirm deleted_at changes as expected and thread is hidden/shown in listings accordingly.

dependencies.purpose: Board for thread.
Thread author.
Create thread to be soft-deleted/restored.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a thread with a non-existent id. Attempt to update and expect a not found error response.
Test that updating a thread with invalid values (e.g., empty title or excessively long title/body, or values not allowed by schema) produces validation errors and does not update data.

dependencies.purpose: Board for valid thread.
Thread author.
Thread to be updated with invalid data.

scenarios.draft: Test soft-deleting a thread by id. Create a thread, call DELETE on its id, and verify the thread's deleted_at is set (by subsequently fetching the thread and checking the deleted_at field).

dependencies.purpose: Board for thread creation.
Thread author.
Create a thread to soft-delete.

scenarios.draft: Test soft-deleting a thread using a non-existent id. Call DELETE with an invalid UUID and verify that the system returns a not found error.

Test repeated soft-deletion of an already soft-deleted thread to ensure idempotency and error-handling is correct. Create and soft-delete a thread, then try soft-deleting it again and verify the outcome (e.g., no error or error indicating already deleted, per platform rules).

dependencies.purpose: Board for thread creation.
Thread author.
Create a thread.
Perform initial soft delete before attempting repeat deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test listing post votes using valid filtering criteria, sorting, and pagination. A post and a member must exist with at least one vote cast by that member on the post. As a prerequisite, create a member, a post, and cast a vote. Query the list of votes using filters on post ID, member ID, vote type, and created_at (date range). Assert that the returned votes match the query criteria and that pagination metadata is present.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member to obtain a valid member ID for vote creation and filtering.
Create a post to have a valid post ID for associating votes and filtering.
Cast a vote by the created member on the created post, ensuring there's at least one record to query.

scenarios.draft: Test listing post votes with filters that intentionally match no results. Use either a nonexistent post or member ID (ensure they do not exist) to filter. The response should be an empty result set with valid pagination metadata. This checks the search function's handling of absence of data.

Test successfully retrieving the details of a post vote by a valid existing ID. Create a member, a post, and have the member vote on the post. Then, retrieve the vote using the returned vote ID and assert that all expected vote details match the creation info.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member to be used for post voting.
Create a post to allow association to the vote.
Cast a post vote and obtain the vote ID to retrieve.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a post vote by an ID that does not exist. Use a UUID that is not associated with any post vote and verify the response is a 404 not found error.

Test casting a new vote for a post by a member with valid data. A member and a post must be created first. Attempt to cast a vote (vote_type among allowed 1,-1,0). Verify that the response returns the created vote and matches the input data (member, post, vote_type, created_at).

dependencies.purpose: Register a member who will cast the post vote.
Create a post for voting.

scenarios.draft: Test attempting to create a post vote for a (post, member) pair that already has a vote. This checks the schema's uniqueness constraint. Create a member and post, cast the initial vote, then attempt to vote again with the same pair. Expect a constraint violation error indicating uniqueness ([discussionboard_post_id, discussionboard_member_id]).

dependencies.purpose: Register a member who will cast post votes.
Create a post to allow post voting.
Cast the first post vote to trigger uniqueness on the second vote.

scenarios.draft: Test attempting to create a post vote with an invalid vote_type value (not 1, -1, or 0). Prepare a member and a post to serve as valid foreign keys, then attempt to vote with an out-of-range value. Expect a validation error for vote_type.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member for voting.
Create a post to receive a vote.

scenarios.draft: Test updating an existing post vote's vote_type (e.g., from upvote to downvote). Create a member, post, and initial vote. Use the update endpoint to change the vote_type, and assert that the update persists in the returned vote entity with other fields unchanged. Check vote uniqueness constraint still holds.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member for post voting.
Create a post to be the subject of voting.
Cast an initial vote in order to update it.

scenarios.draft: Test attempting to update a post vote with an ID that does not exist. Attempt the update using a made-up UUID and validate that the endpoint returns a not found error.

Test attempting to update a post vote with an invalid vote_type value. Create a valid vote, then attempt to update it to an invalid value (not 1, -1, or 0). Confirm a schema validation error is returned and the original value is unchanged.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member for voting.
Create a post for voting.
Create an initial valid post vote to use for the update test.

scenarios.draft: Test deleting an existing post vote by its ID. Prepare a member, post, and vote, then delete the vote. Subsequent lookups of the deleted vote should fail (404), confirming the hard delete.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member for voting.
Create a post to receive votes.
Create a post vote record to be deleted.

scenarios.draft: Test deleting a post vote with a non-existent ID. Attempt the delete with a made-up or random UUID, and verify the system returns an appropriate not found error.

Test listing public member profiles using pagination, filtering by display name, and sorting. Create several members and corresponding public profiles first. Issue a PATCH request supplying pagination parameters and a filter (e.g., display_name contains a substring) to verify that only relevant profiles appear in the returned paginated results. Validate that all returned fields match the schema. This scenario also tests that only public, non-sensitive profile fields are included and no authentication is required.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple member records to reference for profile creation.
Create member profiles associated with different members to populate the listing.

scenarios.draft: Test the member profile list endpoint when there are no profiles in the system. Issue a PATCH request with default parameters and validate that the result set is empty and no error occurs. This verifies correct behavior for empty tables, such as at initial installation, and ensures a zero-result is handled gracefully.

Test filtering member profiles by location using the PATCH endpoint. First, create several member and member profile records with different locations. Then, request a paginated result where location matches a given city or keyword, and assert that only matching profiles are returned according to filter logic. Verify correct results for both matches and no matches, confirming filter accuracy and field matching rules.

dependencies.purpose: Set up test members to be linked with profiles.
Create profiles featuring distinct locations to enable filter-by-location testing.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving an existing member profile by its id. First, create a member and a profile. Then perform a GET with the created profile's id and verify the response contains correct public profile fields as defined by the schema, including id, member_id, display_name, and optional fields (bio, avatar_url, location, website_url). Ensure no sensitive information is included. Confirm successful retrieval and correct formatting for all fields.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member for whom the profile will be created.
Create a profile for the member to later fetch by id.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieval failure when requesting a member profile by a non-existent or already-deleted id. Attempt a GET request with a random or deleted UUID and assert that the system returns an appropriate not found error (e.g., 404). Ensure no data is leaked and error structure aligns with system conventions.

Test successfully creating a member profile record for an existing member. First, create a member account. Then POST to /discussionboard/memberProfiles with required fields, such as member_id and display_name, plus optional fields like bio or avatar_url. Validate successful creation, correct population of all fields, and enforcement of uniqueness constraint (one profile per member). The returned profile must match all schema properties and be publicly accessible.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member record to link the new profile to.

scenarios.draft: Test that creating a second profile for the same member fails with a proper uniqueness violation error. First, create a member and a profile (POST). Then, attempt to create another profile with the same member_id and confirm that the API rejects it with a uniqueness error without side effects. This ensures business rules—one profile per member—are respected.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to use for duplicate profile test.
Create the first profile for the member to establish the conflict for the second creation attempt.

scenarios.draft: Test creation failure when required fields (such as member_id or display_name) are omitted from the POST body. Attempt to create a member profile with missing members or display_name, and confirm the API returns a validation error explaining the missing or invalid input. No profiles should be created as a result.

Test successful update of an existing member profile by id. First, create a member and profile. Then, issue a PUT with new values for one or more updatable fields (e.g., display_name, bio, avatar_url, location, website_url). Confirm the response reflects the updated data, unchanged fields remain correct, and all properties adhere to schema. Verify business rules, such as only allowing updates to fields defined in the schema.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member as the basis for the profile.
Create a member profile to update.

scenarios.draft: Test failure to update a member profile that does not exist. Attempt a PUT to the endpoint with a non-existent profile id and confirm that the system returns a not found error (404) with no side effects. This verifies correct handling of updates for profiles that are missing or already deleted.

Test failure when attempting to update a member profile with invalid field types or unsupported extra properties. Attempt a PUT with data that includes unexpected fields or invalid types for schema properties and assert the system rejects the update with validation errors. Confirm that the profile is not modified and database integrity is preserved.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member and profile, if required, to validate rejection of improper fields.

scenarios.draft: Test successful hard deletion of a member profile by its id. First, create a member and a profile. Then issue a DELETE request to the profile's endpoint and confirm that the operation succeeds. Attempt to retrieve the profile by id afterwards and verify it results in a not found error. This validates clean and irreversible removal.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member and profile to be deleted.
Create the profile to be deleted.

scenarios.draft: Test hard delete operation on a non-existent profile. Issue a DELETE request with a random or already-deleted id and verify that the server responds with an appropriate not found error, and no side effects occur.

Test business rule that only the profile owner or an admin may delete a profile. Attempt to DELETE a profile as a different member, as an unauthorized user, or without authentication and assert the API responds with an authorization error. Profile should remain untouched, verifying correct enforcement of authorization.

dependencies.purpose: Create both the profile owner and a different, non-owner member for cross-deletion testing.
Create profile for owned and unauthorized deletion scenario.

scenarios.draft: Verify that a moderator or admin can retrieve a paginated list of post snapshots filtered by a valid discussionboard_post_id. First, create a post and at least two snapshots for that post using the discussionboard_post_snapshots table. Then perform a PATCH request with a filter for that specific post ID and check that all related snapshots are returned in the response, that each matches the correct post_id, and pagination info is consistent with created rows.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post to associate with post snapshots, ensuring a valid discussionboard_post_id is available.
Create two or more post snapshots to ensure there are records to retrieve during the test.

scenarios.draft: Test that an unauthorized user (without moderator or admin role) receives an error when attempting to list post snapshots. Attempt to PATCH /discussionboard/postSnapshots as a regular member or guest and verify that access is denied (expected: 403 Forbidden or similar error response).

Validate that when no filter is applied in the PATCH request for post snapshots, the endpoint returns all available snapshots, paginated. Create snapshots for multiple posts. Then perform the request without any filters to confirm that the response includes snapshots from all posts and that pagination is correct.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple posts to ensure there are different post_ids for snapshot creation.
Create post snapshots linked to different posts to test aggregate retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Check that a moderator or admin can retrieve a specific post snapshot by its valid id. First, create a post and a post snapshot, then perform a GET on the returned snapshot's id. Verify that the full details match the created snapshot, including correct title, body, and timestamps.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post to use as the associated entity for the snapshot.
Create a post snapshot for retrieval of ID in the subsequent get test.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieval of a post snapshot with an id that does not exist. Attempt a GET on /discussionboard/postSnapshots/{id} using a random but properly formatted UUID not in the database. Expect a 404 Not Found error.
Attempt to fetch a post snapshot with a correct id as an unauthorized user (not a moderator/admin). Confirm that the request is denied and an appropriate error (403 or 401) is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post and at least one snapshot with an authorized user so there is a valid id to target.
Create the snapshot as preparation for fetching with unauthorized credentials.

scenarios.draft: Verify that a moderator or admin can create a post snapshot using all required and permitted schema fields. First, create a valid post, then use the post's id in the snapshot creation request. Confirm that the snapshot is persisted with accurate title, body, editor_member_id, and taken_at timestamp, and that the response contains all expected schema fields.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post for use as the parent reference when creating the snapshot.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to create a post snapshot with a discussionboard_post_id that does not exist. Confirm that the service returns an appropriate error due to foreign key violation, and that no snapshot is created.

Try to create a post snapshot omitting one or more required fields. Expect the endpoint to reject the payload with a validation error, indicating missing required schema fields such as discussionboard_post_id, title, or body.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post to use in a negative test case if needed.

scenarios.draft: Check that a moderator or admin can update the fields of a post snapshot, such as title and body, when supplying only schema-permitted properties. Create a post and a post snapshot; perform a PUT on the snapshot's id to change title and/or body. Verify that the returned data reflects the changes and all schema fields are accurate.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post with which to associate the snapshot.
Create a snapshot to update during the test.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to update a post snapshot using an id that does not exist. Expect a 404 Not Found error and verify that no data is changed in the system.
Attempt an update with extra/invalid payload fields, or missing required fields. Expect the endpoint to reject the request with an appropriate validation error. No update should be performed.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post and associated snapshot for testing invalid update scenarios.
Create the snapshot to target with invalid updates.

scenarios.draft: Test that a moderator or admin can successfully hard-delete a post snapshot. Create a post and a post snapshot, then perform a DELETE on the snapshot's id. Confirm the snapshot is no longer retrievable and deletion is permanent.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post and relate a snapshot for downstream delete action.
Set up the post snapshot to be deleted.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to delete a post snapshot using an id that does not exist, and confirm the API returns an appropriate error (404 Not Found or similar).

Test that deleting a post snapshot as an unauthorized user fails with an error. After setting up a snapshot as an admin or moderator, attempt to delete it as a member or guest. Verify that the service responds with a 403 or similar error, and that the snapshot remains in storage.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post and snapshot as an authorized user then attempt delete as unauthorized.
Setup snapshot to target with unauthorized delete operation.

scenarios.draft: Test listing boards using filter and pagination parameters. First, create several boards with distinct values for categories, sections, names, and status (is_active, is_visible). Then, send a PATCH request providing specific search and filter fields (such as searching by section, category, code, or active/visibility status) and pagination controls. Validate that the response contains only boards matching the criteria, is paginated properly, and no extra or missing boards appear. Test with various filter combinations, empty results, and edge case page limits.

dependencies.purpose: Create several boards with varied properties to provide a dataset for testing filter and pagination scenarios.

scenarios.draft: Test that listing boards without providing any filter returns all existing boards. Create multiple boards, then invoke the PATCH endpoint without search criteria. Verify the response includes all boards that exist in the system. Ensure pagination works if the dataset exceeds page limits, and confirm no boards are missing unexpectedly.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple boards so that the list operation returns a useful set for all-boards retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a single board by its unique ID. Create a board, then use its id to fetch details. Confirm that all returned fields match those initially provided and those generated (like timestamps). The response must contain exactly one board and match schema fields as described.

dependencies.purpose: Create the board and obtain its unique id for use in the GET operation.

scenarios.draft: Test the case where a request is made for a non-existent board id. Attempt to query with a random or already-deleted id, and verify that a not found error or 404 is returned, with no board record in the body.

Test board creation with all required and optional valid fields. Supply proper references for category, section, and set fields like name, code, is_active, is_visible, etc. Confirm the board is created, returned data matches input and schema (including created_at/updated_at), and the board is retrievable via GET and appears in PATCH listing. Test that all business rules and valid parameter types result in successful creation.
Test creating a board while omitting a required field such as name, code, category, or section id. Expect a validation error indicating the missing field and ensure the board is NOT created.

Test creation of two boards with the same code or name (if uniqueness is enforced). First, create a board with a specific code/name; then attempt to create another with the same value. Confirm the second request fails with a uniqueness constraint violation, and the original board remains unaffected.

dependencies.purpose: Create the first board with the code or name to establish the unique constraint for the duplicate test.

scenarios.draft: Test updating an existing board with new valid data (e.g., change name, visibility, description). Ensure the PUT request properly updates only the provided fields and does not affect immutable fields. Confirm the updated board can be retrieved and reflects all changes. Validate timestamps are modified appropriately.

dependencies.purpose: Create the initial board to receive updates, capturing its id for use in update tests.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a board using an id that does not exist. Attempt the update and confirm a not found/404 error is returned with no change to the boards data store.
Test updating a board with invalid field values or with fields that are not allowed by the schema. The API should reject such updates and provide clear validation error responses.

dependencies.purpose: Create a board to provide an updatable id and a basis for field validation scenarios.

scenarios.draft: Test the hard delete of a board using its id. First, create a board; then delete it by id. Confirm that the board is permanently removed (cannot be retrieved via GET or found in the listing). Validate that deletions do not cascade to unrelated boards and the response format matches documentation.

dependencies.purpose: Create the board to have an id available for deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test deleting a non-existent board. Pass an invalid or already-deleted id to DELETE and ensure the operation fails gracefully with an appropriate not found error or a clear message.

Test business logic when deleting a board and then attempting to re-create a new board with the same code. Verify if deletion truly frees up unique constraints (if any) or if certain references prevent immediate reuse. Expect the new board creation to succeed if the constraint is released upon hard delete, or fail if legacy state persists.

dependencies.purpose: Create a board (capturing code value), delete that board, and then use code value in a subsequent creation operation to test uniqueness/constraint release on delete.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of data erasure requests for administrative review. The scenario covers listing all records, searching by status (such as 'pending', 'approved', 'completed'), and using pagination controls to navigate through results. The test should ensure correct enforcement of filters and that results only include actual schema fields. Verifies that only proper fields are used and unintended records (e.g., those outside the filter criteria) are excluded.

dependencies.purpose: Create a test member to generate associated data erasure requests for filtering.
Submit at least one new data erasure request to ensure there is a record to filter/search for.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieval of a single data erasure request's full detail by its valid UUID. Ensures all schema-defined fields are present and match expected values. Verifies that lookup by id returns the correct record for admin or authorized staff review.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account and obtain their id for use in generating a data erasure request.
Create an actual data erasure request and extract its id to perform the lookup.

scenarios.draft: Test error handling for retrieving a data erasure request by using an invalid or non-existent UUID. Expects a 404 or not found error, ensuring the endpoint does not leak data or return unintended error details for non-existent records.

Test the full submission flow of a new data erasure request by an authenticated member. Ensures that a new row is created with 'status' as 'pending', 'requested_at' set to current timestamp, and all appropriate default/null values for reviewed_at, completed_at, and admin_remark. Verifies system assigns the id and blocks extraneous fields. Also ensures request is only permitted if the member is authenticated and does not have an open request.

dependencies.purpose: Register a regular member to simulate a legitimate data erasure request submission.

scenarios.draft: Test the system properly enforces the rule that a member may not have multiple open or pending erasure requests. Submits a new request for a member who already has one in status 'pending' and verifies the API rejects it with a validation or business logic error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account to simulate repeat data erasure requests.
Submit the initial data erasure request to set the status as 'pending'.

scenarios.draft: Test updating the status, reviewed_at, completed_at, and admin_remark fields on a data erasure request by an authorized admin. Covers workflows such as approving or denying a request, marking it complete, and providing remarks for compliance. Ensures only schema fields are updatable and that transitions (pending->approved/completed) are strictly enforced as per business logic.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new member to generate an erasure request for update testing.
Create a data erasure request whose id will be updated in this workflow.

scenarios.draft: Test error handling for attempting to update a non-existent or invalid data erasure request id. Ensures a 404 or business logic error is returned and the system does not process or alter any records inadvertently.

Test the permanent deletion (hard delete) of a data erasure request by an authorized admin or moderator. Confirms the record is irreversibly removed and no longer retrievable, and that only the id is required. Scenario also verifies an authorized role is necessary and no cascading deletes occur to other records.

dependencies.purpose: Create a test member to be the subject of a data erasure request.
Create a data erasure request to later delete by id.

scenarios.draft: Test deleting a data erasure request using a bogus or non-existent id. Check that a proper error (404 or validation error) results and the system is not impacted or leaking sensitive error information.

Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of activity logs. Admins should be able to request logs filtered by event type, member, time range, and combination of entity references (board, thread, post, comment). Verify that only records matching criteria are returned. Confirm pagination reflects actual result sizes and that no unauthorized or non-schema fields can be used as filters. Also test invalid filter parameters are gracefully rejected. This scenario covers navigation, audit review, and compliance queries.

Test fetching a single activity log by id. Positive case: Retrieve an activity log entry created earlier and verify that all schema fields match expected values. Negative case: Attempt to fetch a non-existent or already-deleted activity log id and confirm that a 404 or appropriate not-found error is returned. Confirm that only roles with appropriate permission can access this endpoint if applicable.

dependencies.purpose: Create an activity log record to ensure a known id exists for detail retrieval testing.

scenarios.draft: Test creation of an activity log record by an admin. Provide valid schema-conformant values for all fields (event_type, event_timestamp, member and entity references, event_metadata). Confirm new log is persisted and returned with correct id. Also, attempt creation with missing or malformed required fields and verify appropriate validation errors are returned. Ensure no unspecified fields can be included in the payload. This scenario ensures both standard creation and failure on invalid input are handled as expected.

Test full update of an activity log record by id, changing event_type, event_timestamp, and one or more entity references and event_metadata. Positive flow: Confirm that log is properly updated and new values are saved. Negative flow: Attempt update with missing or invalid fields; attempt update of a non-existent id and verify a not-found or error response is returned. Ensure only schema-approved fields can be edited and extraneous data is rejected.

dependencies.purpose: Create an activity log record so its id can be used for testing the update operation.

scenarios.draft: Test permanent deletion of an activity log by id. First, create a new log record, then delete it by id and confirm the entry is irreversibly removed (cannot be retrieved afterward). Attempt deletion of a non-existent or already-deleted id to confirm a 404 or proper error code is returned. Ensure that only permitted roles can perform this hard delete action if applicable.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure a known activity log record exists for deletion tests.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of trending topics for management or analytics. Cover cases where filters are provided (e.g., by ranking period date or board/thread) and no filters (retrieve all). Include testing default pagination as well as custom limits and page numbers. Confirm correct fields are returned and results match filter/sort criteria. Handle edge case where no records match filters and verify empty result is handled correctly.

Test listing trending topics with an invalid filter or malformed parameter (such as using an unsupported field or invalid data type). Confirm that the API returns a structured validation error indicating the cause and that no internal server error occurs.

Test querying a trending topics page number that exceeds available results (e.g., requesting page 20 when only one page of results exists). API should return an empty array for results and correct pagination metadata without crashing or throwing an error.

Test retrieving the details of a specific trending topic by a valid id. First, create a trending topic, then use its id in the GET request. Verify all fields provided by the schema are present and accurate.

dependencies.purpose: Create a trending topic to obtain a valid id for the get-by-id test.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a trending topic by a non-existent id, ensuring that the API returns a 404 not found error and does not expose internal system details.

Test creating a new trending topic with all required and valid fields (thread_id, board_id, ranking period date, trending score). On success, the API should return the new record with all schema fields correctly populated.
Test creating a trending topic while omitting a required field, such as ranking_period_date. The API should reject the request and return a clear validation error describing the missing field.

Test business logic for preventing duplicate trending topic entries (e.g., for the same thread, board, and ranking period date). First, successfully create a trending topic, then attempt to create another with the same key fields. The API should reject the duplicate with a suitable error.

dependencies.purpose: Create an initial trending topic to use for duplicate entry test.

scenarios.draft: Test updating an existing trending topic by id using valid update data (such as new trending score or updated ranking period). Confirm all changes are reflected in the response and no fields outside the schema can be updated.

dependencies.purpose: Create a trending topic record to update.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a trending topic using a non-existent id. The API should return a not found error and make no changes to the data.

Test updating a trending topic with a payload that violates schema constraints (such as an invalid trending score type or extra fields not in schema). The API must return a validation error without updating the record.

dependencies.purpose: Create a trending topic for controlled update testing with invalid payloads.

scenarios.draft: Test hard-deleting a trending topic by id after creation. Confirm that the record is no longer retrievable and is fully removed from system storage. API should return a success status with no data remaining for the deleted id.

dependencies.purpose: Create a trending topic to use as the delete target.

scenarios.draft: Test attempting to delete a trending topic using a non-existent id. API must respond with a not found error, confirming no cascading effect or server error occurs.

Test listing engagement metrics filtered and paginated by member, board, and engagement date ranges. Set up by creating multiple engagement metric records for different members and boards across several dates to simulate activity. Use the endpoint to filter by a specific member, by board, and by a date range, verifying the results match only the records that fit the search criteria. Check correct handling of pagination (e.g., page 1 and 2 return the correct subsets), and validate total count metadata. Edge case: filter for a member/board/date combination that yields zero results to ensure empty result sets are handled correctly. Also check results when filtering by nullable fields (e.g., member or board is null).

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple engagement metric records for several members and boards to have sample data for listing, filtering, and pagination tests.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving engagement metric details by id. For a success path, create an engagement metric record, then fetch it by its id and verify all returned fields match what was created. For error handling, attempt to fetch engagement metrics with a non-existent id to ensure the endpoint returns a 404 or appropriate error. Edge case: try to fetch an engagement metric after it was deleted to confirm that it is no longer accessible and a not-found error is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create an engagement metric record to retrieve by id.
Test error handling for fetch after deletion by deleting an engagement metric and confirming it cannot be retrieved.

scenarios.draft: Test creating an engagement metric with fully valid data, making sure a new record is created and returned with all the schema fields populated correctly. Test error cases such as required fields missing, invalid types, or constraint violations (e.g., negative post/comment/vote counts, or fields not matching allowed data types). Edge case: attempt to create a metric with the same member/board/date as an existing record if uniqueness is required. Verify that errors are clear and do not create a partial or invalid record.

Test updating an engagement metric by id—changing the posts, comments, or votes counts and possibly changing associated member or board if permitted. Validate success when inputs are valid and all fields are updated as expected. Test error paths: try updating a non-existent id (should return not found), invalid values (e.g., negative numbers, wrong types), and attempt to update with missing required fields. Edge case: update the metric to have null for nullable fields where allowed and confirm correct behavior.

dependencies.purpose: Create an engagement metric to update in the test.

scenarios.draft: Test hard-deleting an engagement metric by id. First, create an engagement metric; then, delete it using this endpoint and verify the response confirms deletion. Attempt to retrieve the deleted record to ensure it is truly removed and an error is returned. Test the edge case where deleting a non-existent or already-deleted id returns the appropriate error.

dependencies.purpose: Create an engagement metric to be deleted during this test.
Validate that the engagement metric was actually deleted by querying for it after deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a paginated, filtered list of member notification preference records. Create several notification preference records for different members and codes, each with a unique combination of email, in-app, and browser notification flags. Then perform a PATCH request to the endpoint with various filters (by member_id, code, email_enabled, etc.), verify that only matching results are returned. The scenario also tests pagination (limit/offset/page parameters) and ensures no soft-deleted records are included (all are active by default). Different filter combinations, sorting order, and pagination should be verified for correctness.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple notification preference records for different members and codes to ensure a realistic filterable dataset for validation.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a specific notification preference by its valid id. First, create a distinct notification preference record and extract the returned id. Use the GET endpoint to fetch the record by id, verify all fields (member_id, code, email_enabled, inapp_enabled, browser_enabled, created_at, updated_at) are returned as expected. Confirm that the data matches the original values used on creation.

dependencies.purpose: Create a notification preference to provide a valid id for direct lookup and ensure test isolation.

scenarios.draft: Test error handling when retrieving a notification preference by a non-existent id. Use a randomly generated UUID (not linked to any record) with the GET endpoint. Verify that a 404 or appropriate not-found error is returned, and no partial data is disclosed.

Test creating a notification preference with valid data. Prepare sample member_id, code, and all boolean preference flags. Submit the POST request and verify the returned record includes all schema fields and values match those sent, plus valid id, created_at, and updated_at. Check that the record is retrievable via GET and matches expected data.

Test error response when attempting to create a duplicate notification preference for the same member_id and code. First, create a preference record for a member and code; then attempt to create another with the same member_id and code (even if notification channels differ). Confirm that the second operation returns an error due to unique key constraint. This validates proper enforcement of no-duplicate-notification-preference-per-member/code-pair business logic.

dependencies.purpose: First create a unique notification preference, then attempt a duplicate for the same (member_id, code) combination to trigger the expected error.

scenarios.draft: Test that creation fails with an appropriate validation error when required fields are omitted (e.g., omitting code or member_id). Attempt to create a record with missing required fields and verify that validation errors are returned, with no record created.

Test updating notification channel preferences for an existing record. Create a preference, then update one or more of the channel flags (email_enabled, inapp_enabled, browser_enabled) via PUT for the record's id. Verify the response matches the updated values and updated_at is adjusted. Confirm retrieval by GET returns the updated state.

dependencies.purpose: Create a notification preference to have a valid id and initial flag state for update testing.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a notification preference using a non-existent id. Attempt a valid update operation with a random UUID not associated with any record and verify that the API returns a not found or error status, without performing any updates.

Test update operation with invalid input: use invalid or missing field values (such as an empty string for code, missing required fields, or wrong data types). Expect the service to return validation errors or reject the update, with no change made to the data.

dependencies.purpose: Create a valid notification preference record for update negative testing, then attempt to update with invalid or missing fields.

scenarios.draft: Test the successful hard deletion of a notification preference. Create a preference, then delete it by id. Confirm that the record is removed and that subsequent attempts to retrieve it by GET return a not-found error. Ensure the operation does not affect other preferences or related entities.

dependencies.purpose: Create a notification preference as the target for deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test handling deletion with a non-existent id. Attempt deletion using a random UUID not matching any record. Verify the API responds with an appropriate error or not-found status and does not affect existing preferences.

Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of discussion posts by supplying a specific thread ID and limiting results to a set number per page. The scenario should ensure only posts belonging to the selected thread are returned, pagination metadata is accurate, and edge cases such as requesting beyond the last page or an empty thread return valid results. The list must accurately reflect the 'is_deleted' status for soft-deleted posts. Ensure that sorting and filtering combinations are supported as described in the business logic.

dependencies.purpose: Create a thread that posts will belong to, ensuring a valid thread ID for filter testing.
Create at least one member who will be the author of test posts. Required for valid member_id in post creation.
Create a board to be referenced by thread and post creation (to fulfill board_id foreign key relationships).
Create multiple posts with various members, in the created thread, to fill several pagination pages. Include some posts marked as is_deleted=true to test display logic.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a specific post by ID, ensuring the response includes all fields. Confirm normal posts are returned fully, and that a post marked as is_deleted=true is still retrievable (with the deletion status reflected). Confirm that retrieving a non-existent post ID returns a 404 error. Test behavior for both regular members and moderators (if permissions ever restrict fields).

dependencies.purpose: Create a thread to associate a post with (required for valid post creation).
Create a member to serve as post author.
Create a board for valid post creation.
Create one normal and one is_deleted=true post for retrieval tests.

scenarios.draft: Test creating discussion posts with valid and invalid data. First, attempt to create a post using all valid fields, confirming the new row is created and fields match input. Then, attempt post creation with missing required fields (such as missing thread ID, board ID, or title), and verify that validation errors are returned. Test constraint failure when referencing non-existent thread, board, or member IDs. Ensure that unexpected fields are rejected and only atomic schema fields are accepted.

dependencies.purpose: Create a valid thread for post association.
Create a member to be used as post author.
Create a board which correct posts will reference as discussionboard_board_id.

scenarios.draft: Test updating an existing post. Validate changing the title and/or body, and setting is_deleted to true for soft-deletion. Confirm response fields reflect changes and updated_at is properly adjusted. Attempt to update with invalid data (e.g., missing required fields, updating with non-existent post ID) and confirm errors are returned. Ensure is_deleted flag transitions are honored by soft delete status.

dependencies.purpose: Create a valid thread for associating the post.
Create a member to serve as the original author.
Create a board for post association.
Create a post to retrieve and then update for this scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test soft-deleting a post by setting its is_deleted flag to true using the DELETE endpoint. Confirm that after soft-deletion, the post still exists but is flagged as deleted (and can be retrieved by GET for audit purposes). Attempt to soft-delete a non-existent post and confirm that the system returns the appropriate error. Test safe multiple DELETE invocations on an already-deleted post and verify idempotency or relevant response.

dependencies.purpose: Create a thread to associate with the test post.
Create a member to author the test post.
Create a board for the post.
Create the post to be deleted in this scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of comment reports for moderation review. The test should create multiple comments by different members and generate several comment reports against them using various report types and reasons. Use the listing API to: (a) retrieve all reports paginated, (b) filter by a specific comment ID to see only related reports, (c) filter by report type to validate the filtering, and (d) paginate the results to verify correct limits and offsets. Ensure only schema fields are accepted for searching/filtering and verify that the results reflect the correct records as per the filters and pagination.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple comment reports for different comments, report types, and members to ensure relevant test data exists for filtering and pagination tests.
Create another comment report referencing a different report type or reason for broader filter coverage.
Create target comment records to report against; valid comments must exist to test reporting and listing relationships.
Register member accounts who will create comments and submit reports.

scenarios.draft: Test fetching a specific comment report by its id. First, create a comment report with known field values. Request the report by its id using the detail endpoint and verify that all returned fields (including comment id, member id, report type id, reason, and created_at) match the initial creation. Verify the endpoint returns the report when the id exists, and data matches expectations.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment report with traceable values (e.g., known member id, report type id, comment id, and non-null reason) to acquire a valid id for the fetch-by-id test.

scenarios.draft: Test the error scenario when attempting to fetch a comment report by a non-existent id. Use a random or deleted UUID that does not correspond to any report. Verify the system returns a 404 or appropriate not found error and does not leak additional information. Ensure this scenario helps validate robust error handling for missing records.

Test creating a new comment report with all required valid information. Set up a scenario where a member has posted a comment and another member files a report on it, selecting a valid report type and providing a non-null reason. Validate that creation succeeds, the report record is returned with correct fields, and the entry is available for future queries.

dependencies.purpose: Create the comment that will be reported.
Ensure valid member records exist—one for the comment author, another for the reporting member.
Create or confirm a valid report type for use in the report.

scenarios.draft: Test failure to create a comment report when the required reason field is omitted or null. Attempt to submit a report without specifying a non-null reason and validate that the API responds with a validation error indicating the reason is required.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment as the target for the report.
Ensure reporter and comment author members are available.
Ensure a valid report type exists for testing invalid submissions.

scenarios.draft: Test creating a comment report for a nonexistent comment id. Attempt to submit a report referencing a random or deleted comment UUID. The API should reject the report with an error due to foreign key or referential integrity violation.

dependencies.purpose: Set up a member who will act as the reporting user.
Provide a valid report type for use in testing referential integrity.

scenarios.draft: Test updating an existing comment report, modifying allowed fields like reason and report type id (if schema allows). First, create a report, then update its reason, member id, or report type id, and verify that the changes persist and are reflected in the returned record.

dependencies.purpose: Create a base comment report that can be updated in the test.

scenarios.draft: Test failure when updating a comment report to reference an invalid or nonexistent comment id. Attempt the update referencing a deleted or random UUID and verify the API returns an integrity or not found error, without corrupting or updating the original report.

dependencies.purpose: First create a valid comment report to update in this negative test.

scenarios.draft: Test successful deletion of a comment report by id. Create a report, then invoke the deletion API and verify the following: (a) the API confirms deletion, (b) attempting to fetch the same report by id returns a not found error, and (c) the report no longer appears in subsequent listing/filtering results.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment report to be deleted.

scenarios.draft: Test deleting a comment report by a non-existent id. Attempt the delete operation with a random or already-deleted UUID and verify the API responds with an appropriate not found error, with no side effects on other comment reports.

Test retrieval of a paginated and filtered list of notification templates. The test should cover scenarios where search criteria are provided (e.g., template name keyword), filters are applied (e.g., only active templates), and pagination options are set (various page sizes and numbers). Also verify results are compliant with schema, cover both the case where results are returned and where no template matches the filters. Ensure only schema-defined fields are referenced and that the user has admin privileges for the operation.

dependencies.purpose: Create several diverse notification templates (different names, codes, and active statuses) for list/search scenario coverage before running search and pagination tests.

scenarios.draft: Test successful retrieval of a single notification template when provided with a valid template ID. The scenario involves creating a notification template, retrieving it by its ID, and verifying that all fields are accurately returned according to schema with correct values.

dependencies.purpose: Create a notification template and use its ID to validate single-template retrieval.
